$comment: D4.22 — VALIDATION OF THE DISCOVERY METHOD ITSELF, AND ITS FALSIFICATION.
D4.21 left a question: are the 108 clauses the semantic detector cleared actually clear? Three
experiments answer it, and they agree.
EXPERIMENT 1 — STRUCTURAL DETECTION. A dependency graph already exists in the clause library:
306 edges, 168 clauses declaring `depends_on`. Walking it toward clauses with an UNDECIDED
treatment recovers CORE_SURVIVAL_001 --depends_on--> CORE_TERMINATION_001 without reading a word
of the survival clause. It also finds MSA_GOVERNANCE_BODY_001. It finds nothing else, because
inheritance can only reach as far as the six open decisions extend. HIGH PRECISION, NEAR-ZERO
RECALL, and that is a property of the method rather than a property of the corpus.
EXPERIMENT 2 — READING A SAMPLE. Twelve of the UNDETERMINED clauses were read rather than
scanned. Seven carry a real N-party question. That is a false-negative rate around 58 percent in
the population the detector had cleared.
EXPERIMENT 3 — VOCABULARY ABLATION. The characteristic words were removed from six clauses known
to be cardinality-sensitive. FIVE OF SIX BECAME UNDISCOVERABLE. Only CORE_SURVIVAL_001 survived,
and only through the dependency graph. The detectors succeed because they see the words.
THE CAUSE, WHICH IS ARCHITECTURAL RATHER THAN LEXICAL:
This corpus is drafted in NAMED ROLES — Client and Consultant, Borrower and Lender, Assignor
and Assignee, Fiduciary and Processor. A role-named clause is implicitly bilateral and never
says so. 'The Client shall notify the Consultant' carries exactly the same N-party question
as 'either Party shall notify the other', and announces none of it.
So marker-based discovery cannot work here, and no further tuning of the vocabulary will fix it.
The 42-percent and 89-percent precision figures from D4.21 measured a method that was answering
a different question from the one asked.
THE INVERSION THIS FORCES. Stop trying to DISCOVER the relevant clauses; the base rate is high
and the signal is absent. Instead DISCHARGE the irrelevant ones, because that set is small,
closed and characterisable: definitions, interpretation, severability, counterparts, governing
law, and other rules about the instrument rather than about who signed it. Every other clause in
an N-party-admissible family is PRESUMED RELEVANT until positively discharged.
This changes the burden of proof and therefore the meaning of the backlog. It does not classify
anything, and no clause was modified.

read_sample.method: Twelve UNDETERMINED clauses, chosen deterministically (top six by family exposure, then every twelfth) so the sample is reproducible rather than favourable.

adjudications.question: 'Each Party shall, at the reasonable request and cost of the requesting Party' — with three parties, is assistance owed to each other party severally?
adjudications.missed_because: Contains 'Party' twice and never 'the other Party'. Invisible to the pronoun scan AND to every semantic mechanism.

adjudications.question: Renewal 'unless the Parties expressly agree in writing' — all of them, or a majority?
adjudications.missed_because: The COLLECTIVE_DECISION pattern required 'agreed by the Parties'; the text says 'agree'. Missed on an inflection.

adjudications.question: Work product 'shall vest exclusively in the Client' — where two parties commission or two create, who owns?
adjudications.missed_because: Written entirely in named roles. No party pronoun appears.

adjudications.question: 'Failure by the Principal Debtor to pay' — with co-borrowers, does one default trigger against all?
adjudications.missed_because: Named roles again. This is the PAIRWISE_RIGHT question in the finance family.

adjudications.question: 'The Borrower undertakes' — with co-borrowers, are the covenants joint, several, or joint and several?
'Without the Fiduciary's prior written consent' — joint controllers are ordinary under the DPDP Act, 2023; whose consent then?
Co-owners of copyright assigning jointly — Copyright Act, 1957 s.19 requires the assignment to state its terms, and s.18 governs who may assign.
adjudications.missed_because: Named roles; and D4.21 had deliberately narrowed `assign` to exclude property assignments, which excluded this one correctly as to succession and incorrectly as to ownership.

adjudications.reason: Defines documents and terms. The definitional mechanism does not change with the number of parties.
Operates on provisions, not on parties: a provision is modified or deleted regardless of how many people signed.
A recital generated from intake. Whether a trilateral purpose needs different wording is a drafting question, not obviously a legal one.
Bilateral trade terms in named roles. Who pays whom with three parties depends on what the third party is, which the clause cannot know.
Acceptance by one of several clients binding the rest is plausibly a real question and plausibly a role question. Not settled by reading alone.

result.false_negative_rate: 7 of 12 — about 58 percent of the population the detector had cleared

ablation.method: Characteristic vocabulary removed from six clauses already known to be cardinality-sensitive — 'either/the other/neither/both Party', 'between the Parties', 'equally', 'waiver', 'assign' — then re-detected.

results.note: The only survivor, and it survives through the dependency graph rather than through any text. This is the case the whole design was built around.

ablation.verdict: FIVE OF SIX LOST. The detectors have not solved the problem; they recognise the words. Only the structural detector is vocabulary-independent, and it reaches two clauses out of 184.

conclusion: Reported separately, as required, rather than as one coverage figure:
precision of the D4.21 detector   89% after repair (3 false positives in 27)
recall of the D4.21 detector      unmeasurable by detection; ≈42% by reading sample
ablation survival                 1 of 6, and that one only structurally
The discovery defect is SYSTEMIC and is not fixable by a better word list. The corpus is drafted
in named roles, and a role-named bilateral clause carries the same N-party question as a
pronoun-named one while announcing none of it.

methodological_rule.rule: N-party relevance is PRESUMED for every clause reachable by an N-party-admissible family, unless evidence establishes irrelevance. Detection may DISCHARGE a clause; detection may not CERTIFY relevance.
why: D4.22 established this by three independent experiments rather than by argument: the ablation lost
five of six known-sensitive clauses once their vocabulary was removed; reading twelve cleared
clauses found seven real questions; and the only vocabulary-independent detector reaches two
The asymmetry is the point. A detector that fires is weak evidence of relevance, because it fires
on words rather than mechanisms — PARTY_ROLE_VARIANCE fired on 25 of 25. A detector that stays
silent is NO evidence of irrelevance, because the corpus is drafted in named roles and a
role-named bilateral clause announces nothing. So detection can only ever be used in the
direction where a false answer is cheap: to propose candidates, never to close them.
consequences: NOT_CLASSIFIED means NOT YET SEMANTICALLY DISCHARGED. It does not mean 'probably irrelevant',
and any report that treats it as a clean bill of health is misreporting the state of the system.
Discharge requires POSITIVE evidence per clause — that the rule is about the instrument rather
than about who signed it. Absence of a marker is not that evidence.
Precision, recall and ablation survival are reported SEPARATELY and never blended. D4.22 showed
exactly why: a detector can be 89 percent precise while being structurally incapable of measuring
its own recall on this corpus, and one combined figure would hide that.

accounting.wrong: 161 unclassified — read as 161 unknowns, or worse as 161 probably-fine
right: |     keep their existing and distinct meanings
note: The denominator did not change and neither did the states. What changed is the DEFAULT: a
clause is in scope until discharged, so the 161 is a backlog of presumptively-relevant
clauses rather than a pile of unknowns. That is a more honest ceiling and a worse-sounding
one, which is the usual sign it is the true one.

engine_hypotheses_falsified.hypothesis: A general treatment-level CONDITIONALITY mechanism is needed, because decisions gate one another.
engine_hypotheses_falsified.falsified_by: 30 ordered pairs measured: 0 DETERMINES, 1 GATES, 6 CONSTRAINS, 23 INDEPENDENT.
engine_hypotheses_falsified.conclusion: One gating edge is not a case for an engine. Model named edges; revisit if a second GATES or any DETERMINES edge appears.

engine_hypotheses_falsified.hypothesis: A general CROSS-TREATMENT CONSISTENCY engine is needed, because independently admissible treatments can jointly produce an incoherent instrument.
falsified_by: The MSA/founders cap-indemnity inconsistency does not reproduce in the guarantee family: 2 of 2
Two distinct reasons, and conflating them would have produced the right conclusion by the wrong
mechanism. First, the guarantee family DRAFTS the interaction from both ends. Second, Contract Act
s.146 does not resolve the conflict — it allocates as between co-sureties while the cap bounds the
creditor's recovery under s.128's 'unless otherwise provided'. Different axes cannot contradict.
Testing that rather than assuming it is what separated the finding from a plausible story.
engine_hypotheses_falsified.conclusion: The reusable defect is a missing same-axis interaction RULE, and the remedy is authored legal treatment rather than a detector. An engine would detect a defect that one sentence of ordinary drafting prevents.

engine_hypotheses_falsified.hypothesis: The guarantee interaction sentence can be ported to the five affected families as one reusable treatment.
falsified_by: The condition was that the semantics be genuinely identical. They are not, and the evidence is
mechanical: the shipped cap measures 'the total consideration paid under this Agreement', and NDA
and FOUNDERS_AGREEMENT collect no consideration field of any kind.
Folding a mutual confidentiality indemnity into a cap with no measurable referent does not limit
the indemnity — it erases it. The same sentence that is a real limit in a guarantee is an erasure
engine_hypotheses_falsified.conclusion: Recorded as an UNDECIDED decision with three candidate directions and per-family analysis. Nothing attached, no clause text changed.
